editorNote: A lean day: a claimed AI-generated proof of a famous conjecture that the experts are still checking, a small open model with big coding claims, a self-editing-weights paper, a regulator circling a chip giant, and one tidy database optimization. Several results are self-reported and unreplicated.

stories.headline: Levent Alpöge claims Anthropic models proved the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, with 17.4 million lines of Lean
stories.summary: Alpöge says Anthropic models produced a proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, which implies the Riemann Hypothesis, accompanied by 17.4 million lines of Lean code. Scott Aaronson expects it to stand but is 'not 100% sure' and notes Lean has had kernel bugs.
stories.whyItMatters: A Lean certificate makes checking mechanical, but the proof is unreviewed by the community; Aaronson says no AI result with a Lean certificate has been retracted so far.

sourceLinks.title: Scott Aaronson, The stochastic parrots have apparently proved the Riemann Hypothesis

stories.headline: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini, a 26.4B-parameter open-weights MoE with 3.4B active
stories.summary: The looped-transformer model runs its middle layers three times per token and fits in about 20GB. The company reports 48.2% on DeepSWE v1.1 and 79.2% on SWE-bench Verified, and concedes it trails Qwen3.8-27B on MultiChallenge and ComplexConstraints.
stories.whyItMatters: Strong coding scores are claimed from a model that runs on a 32GB Mac, though all figures are the company's own.

stories.headline: Paper: a 27B language model can rewrite its own weights without gradients, gaining 6.6 points on unseen problems
stories.summary: The authors give an open 27B model its weights and graded answers and let it edit itself; they report a 6.6-point gain on unseen problems and recovery of a damaged copy to over 80% of original accuracy. Smaller models in one family broke themselves or made no useful edit.
stories.whyItMatters: The results are the authors' own, unreplicated claims, and the effect appears to depend on scale.

sourceLinks.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights (arXiv:2611.21885)

stories.headline: Reuters: SEC's Nvidia probe is examining potential accounting issues; shares closed down 14%
stories.summary: Two people briefed told Reuters SEC enforcement staff are scrutinizing Nvidia's accounting; Reuters could not determine when the inquiry opened or which issues are involved. The SEC declined to comment, and Reuters notes investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing.
stories.whyItMatters: The probe adds to Nvidia's legal exposure, which already includes a Justice Department review of its $12.9 billion Hugging Face deal.

sourceLinks.title: US SEC's Nvidia probe is examining potential accounting issues - MarketScreener (Reuters)

stories.headline: Valkey 9.2 swaps the sorted-set skiplist for a B+ tree, cutting per-member overhead by up to 43%
stories.summary: In a 5-million-member test, ordered-index overhead fell from 50.3 to 28.5 bytes for sequential inserts and to 32.0 for random ones. ZADD throughput rose 105% on a pre-merge branch; OBJECT ENCODING now reports 'btree'.
stories.whyItMatters: Commands are unchanged, but tooling that checks for the 'skiplist' encoding string needs updating; the release is still in RC and benchmarks were not rerun after merge.
